clue.text: "My shout," Isaac admitted

indicators.note: to be admitted is to be let inside, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: Ike is a pet form of the name Isaac

explanation.surface: Someone claims the round of drinks while Isaac owns up to something.
explanation.walkthrough: "My shout" reads as offering to buy a round; the definition is just "My" as an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild exclamations of surprise or astonishment, interchangeable as interjections.

clue.text: Lively piece about Chief Information Officer supporting reduced cost

indicators.note: reduced means cut down, so the word loses its final letter
in a down entry a supporting piece holds up from below, so it comes last

explanation.surface: A bright tune about an executive backing budget cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: A capriccio is a free-form, sprightly instrumental composition in music.

clue.text: Recalled vehicles unit only partly operational

indicators.note: only partly means just a portion of these words is taken
recalled things are called back, so the letters are read backwards

blocks.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A unit of recalled cars is only partly working.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in use is currently working or being employed rather than idle.

clue.text: Brunel offers quote in hearing, making sense

indicators.note: in hearing means as it would be heard spoken out loud

blocks.note: Brunel is the setter, who would say I
to offer a quote is to cite

explanation.surface: The engineer Brunel quotes something at a public hearing, talking sense.
explanation.walkthrough: Brunel is this puzzle's setter, so he stands for I.
explanation.definitionFit: Vision is one of the five bodily senses, alongside hearing, smell, taste and touch.

clue.text: One's wearing amulet with a power to inspire

indicators.note: something being worn sits inside its wearer, so the first piece goes into the next word

blocks.note: an amulet is a lucky charm
one = I, plus the 's read as is

explanation.surface: Someone sports a lucky amulet that supposedly lends them a magical power.
explanation.definitionFit: Charisma is the compelling personal magnetism that draws devotion and motivates other people.

clue.text: Using hard clue, tire poor, confused solver

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the collected letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A weary, baffled crossword solver struggles with a tough clue.
explanation.walkthrough: "Solver" looks like the person doing this puzzle; it means a solver of crimes.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's Belgian detective cracks murder mysteries, so he is a fictional crime-solver.

clue.text: Screw up and plan again

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: screw is British prison slang for a warder

explanation.surface: Make a mess of something and have to sketch it out again.
explanation.walkthrough: "Screw up" reads as botch; screw is slang for a prison guard.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraw a map or scheme is to design or sketch it afresh.

clue.text: Setter and Elsie, seen regularly together, initially go steady

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every second letter
initially here means at the start, so that piece is placed in front

blocks.note: to have a go is to have a stab
second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: The setter and Elsie keep meeting, and at first they go steady.
explanation.walkthrough: "Go steady" looks like a phrase about dating; "go" is a try, and "steady" alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stabilise something is to make it firm and secure, holding it fixed.

clue.text: What might be amber beer, served at right temperature

explanation.surface: An amber-coloured beer is served at just the right temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: Amber suggests the colour of the beer; it is a level of warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Warning levels are graded by colour, with amber signalling heightened readiness before red.

clue.text: Writer rings Oxford University lecturer about composer

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the writer goes around what follows

blocks.note: a pen is a writing instrument
L is the abbreviation for lecturer

explanation.surface: A writer telephones an Oxford don concerning some composer.
explanation.walkthrough: "Rings" reads as phoning, but it means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Poulenc was a twentieth-century French musician, member of the group Les Six.

clue.text: Argued with X suppressing speech by Miliband perhaps

indicators.note: in a down entry to suppress is to sit on top, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: Ed Miliband, the British Labour politician, so speech by him is Ed's words

explanation.surface: Someone was argued with over a speech that was quashed, possibly by a Labour leader.
explanation.definitionFit: To cross swords is an idiom meaning to quarrel or dispute, from duelling.

clue.text: Send out judge to collar a policeman

indicators.note: to collar someone is to grab them and hold them in, so the judging word encloses the rest

explanation.surface: A court official is dispatched to arrest a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to emit or give off, as heat or light spreads outward from a source.

clue.text: Reserve in backward old tribespeople

indicators.note: backward tells us to read the little word in from right to left

blocks.note: ice is coolness or reserve of manner
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A reserve of people in some backward land is home to an ancient tribe.
explanation.walkthrough: "in" looks like a link but supplies letters itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic people of ancient Britain, led by Boudicca against Roman rule.

clue.text: He's making eyes at our Lucy, oddly, is Dicky

indicators.note: oddly asks for the letters in odd-numbered positions of the name
dicky means shaky or unsound, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A man is flirting with our Lucy, and he is a bit of a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: "Making eyes at" suggests flirting; the definition stops at "eyes", since the answer literally manufactures them.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocularist is a craftsman who fabricates and fits artificial glass or acrylic replacements for lost eyeballs.

clue.text: Stylish lady in small city

explanation.surface: A fashionable woman is found in some little town.
explanation.walkthrough: CHICHESTER is a cathedral city in West Sussex, one of England's smaller cities.
explanation.definitionFit: Chichester has city status thanks to its cathedral but a population of only about thirty thousand.

clue.text: Arrogantly cutting queen, very disrespectfully

indicators.note: cutting means removing, so the named letters are taken out

explanation.surface: Snubbing the queen arrogantly was a very rude thing to do.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means irreverent or lacking respect, especially towards God or sacred things.

clue.text: Time is swift, maybe

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for a prison sentence, as in doing time
second meaning: a swift is one example of a winged creature

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as "time flies"; in fact time here is a jail term, and "doing bird" is British slang for serving one.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird is rhyming-slang shorthand for a prison term, and a swift is a type of fast-flying avian.

clue.text: Cover version of the duets succeeded

indicators.note: a new version is a reworking, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cover version of the duets was a hit.
explanation.walkthrough: "Cover version" is music talk; "Cover" alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dust sheet is a large cloth draped over furniture to protect it.

clue.text: Mounting disputes about old postal service providing interim solutions

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes around the other
in a down entry, mounting means climbing, so the letters run upwards

blocks.note: the former General Post Office in Britain

explanation.surface: Growing rows over the old postal service lead to temporary fixes.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopgaps are temporary measures used until something better is found.

clue.text: O love, I forgot to mention ... oh dear ...

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
a postscript adds what the writer forgot to say

explanation.surface: A lover's letter trails off with an afterthought and a sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are little exclamations of dismay used on making a mistake or seeing a mishap.

clue.text: Being quick with going for oxygen, see a doctor first

indicators.note: one thing going for another means it is swapped out and replaced

blocks.note: to see an event is to witness it
W is the abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Speedy treatment: substitute oxygen, but first get a doctor to see you.
explanation.walkthrough: "Being quick" sounds like physical speed, but the answer is quickness of hand or wit; "with" is not a link but supplies a letter to be swapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroitness is deftness or skill, the state of being nimble and clever with hands or mind.

clue.text: A German boy's taken recalled book

indicators.note: being taken in means held inside, so the German word goes within the other
recalled means called back, so the whole is read backwards

explanation.surface: A German lad has borrowed a library book he has been asked to return.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel is a book of the Old Testament, named after its prophet.

clue.text: Warrant ordered to arrest OJ - long battle results

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so those letters are rearranged
arresting someone takes them in and holds them, so the other letters wrap around

explanation.surface: A warrant is issued for O J Simpson's arrest, and a lengthy legal fight ensues.
explanation.walkthrough: OJ evokes the Simpson trial; here it is just two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The war between Greeks and Trojans over Helen lasted ten years in legend.

clue.text: They're short on stage 4 components, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means as reported by word of mouth, so the sound matters

blocks.note: four is made up of two twos

explanation.surface: Parts of the fourth stage of some project are running short.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stage 4" reads as a phase; the stage is a theatre, and 4 is two plus two.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutus are the short stiff skirts worn by ballerinas when performing.

clue.text: Senses opportunity to return incomplete models

indicators.note: incomplete means only part of these words is used, the letters across the gap
returning means going back, so the run of letters is read from right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Someone senses a chance to send back unfinished scale models.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to model for an artist or photographer is to sit or stand in position for them.

clue.text: Deal with phone company during brief stay

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped
during means in the middle of, so the company goes inside

blocks.note: EE is a British mobile network

explanation.surface: Handle the phone company during a short stopover.
explanation.definitionFit: To see to a task is an idiom for attending to it or handling it.

clue.text: More scrumptious stunner has sex on rebound

indicators.note: something on the rebound bounces back, so the word comes in the other way
to have is to hold, so the stunning word holds the other inside

blocks.note: a Taser is a stun gun
it is a coy word for sex

explanation.surface: A beautiful woman has a fling on the rebound after a break-up.
explanation.walkthrough: "Stunner" suggests a beauty, but it is a stun gun.
explanation.definitionFit: Tastier is the comparative of tasty, meaning more delicious or appetising to eat.

clue.text: Drugs rumoured to accompany gin, possibly, in swinging bar

indicators.note: a rumour is word of mouth, so we go by how the letters are spoken

blocks.note: a gin is a kind of snare
E is ecstasy, so drugs are Es

explanation.surface: Rumours of drugs taken with gin in a nightclub where people swing.
explanation.walkthrough: "Gin" and "bar" suggest drinking; a gin is also an animal trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a horizontal crossbar hung on ropes, used by circus acrobats.

clue.text: Treasure Island viewer?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone watching a film of the Stevenson story
setter's reading: the pirate's telescope used in the novel, which also names a hill and Silver's inn

explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's novel the treasure is located by bearings from a hill named after this instrument, and Long John Silver keeps an inn of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A spyglass is a small hand-held telescope, a seafaring prop strongly associated with pirate tales.

clue.text: Put in order - right old idiot's got order wrong way round

indicators.note: the two short pieces named first are to be placed in the opposite sequence to the clue

explanation.surface: A proper old fool has jumbled things up while trying to tidy.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiot (ASS) has RT and O, but with their order swapped to O, RT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to classify or arrange things into groups by kind.
